en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The goal is to gain knowledge of basic economic and political context of the development of agriculture and forestry sectors as multifunctional mission and directly linked to the use of natural resources in a globalizing environment of agribusiness.Students will learn about general and specific characteristics of the agricultural and forestry sectors and verifies the ability to interpret in economic terms obtained knowledge of the specifics market factors of production especially with regard to the impact of land as a basic factor of production (valuation principles and factors of pricing). They will gain an overview of the key indicators of economic analysis and learn to apply and interpret the specific examples. Course content: 1. Theoretical basis, subject, concepts, categories (allowance 6/0) a. The specifics of agriculture and forestry, economic interpretation in context, productive and non-productive functions b. Manifestations of globalization in the agricultural sector, forestry-wood complex, agribusiness c. Global and regional context of agribusiness 2. Markets in agribusiness, types of markets, agencies, reciprocal links, category (allowance 12/0) a. Markets of products and services, specifics of the demand and supply formation, market equilibrium b. Factor market, price formation, economic rent and transfer earnings, soil as a basic factor of production, ovaluation of quality, principles and pricing factors c. Economic differentiation in the primary production businesses (agriculture and forestry) and the role of downstream stages of processing 3. Evaluation of position and performance of the industry (allowance 4/13) a. Selected performance indicators b. Information resources for evaluation c. Analysis and interpretation of performance indicators

en.label: [section] Assessment methods:
en.content: Students need to attend at least 80% of classes and seminars to obtain access into the exam. During the semester students will complete a task with several section. At the end of the semster students are assessed on the written submission and the presentation of the task. This makes up 30% of the final mark. The exam mark makes up the balance 70% of the final mark. The overall assessment symbol (the sum of points from the task and written exam) is as follows: A: 100 - 75 % B: 74 - 68 % C: 67 - 62 % D: 61 - 56 % E: 55 - 50 % Less than 50 % is a fail.
